title: A turned or reshaped layer has no thin line along its edges at any zoom
goal: A layer that has been turned, skewed or distorted shows a thin grey line along its outline where its own pixels meet what is under it, most visible zoomed out (the user's report: a Copied Selection of white with a red shape, turned and reshaped, on a white Background at 79 percent; the white-on-white edge should be invisible and is drawn as a faint line). Transformed layers must blend into what is under them exactly as the same pixels would unturned: no seam at any zoom, angle or reshape, on canvas and in export.
notes: User, 2026-11-03 (intake), screenshot queue/audits/2026-11-03-edge-seam-report.png (annotated by the user: 'Thin artifacts on edges after a rotation when zoomed out'): Photonz Dev, Image, layers 'Copied Selection' over 'Background' (locked), canvas 1026 x 831 at 79 percent. The Copied Selection is a white rectangle holding a red rounded shape, turned and reshaped with the new selection modes; a faint grey hairline runs along its outer edge across the white Background. Related renderer pieces: DocumentRenderer (layer transform, the warp / four-corner map added in c2dc5891 'Skew & distort reshapes the picture'), CIPerspectiveTransform for the reshape and 3D.
acceptance: Reproduce: the user's case (a marquee copy of a white area holding a red shape, pasted, turned about 15 degrees and reshaped with Skew & distort, over a white Background) at 25, 50, 79, 100 and 200 percent, and in an export at 1x and 2x. MEASURE the seam: the largest difference from pure white along the layer's outline, in levels, before and after, in the audit with crops.

Find the cause in the render path for a transformed layer (the 2D turn, the Skew & distort reshape through the four-corner perspective map, and the 3D path): likely edge samples blended with transparent black (an un-clamped source resampled at its edge), straight versus premultiplied alpha mixed up, or the canvas downscale filtering the layer's edge on its own before it is composited. Say which, with the evidence.

Fixed: along the outline of a white layer on white, no pixel differs from white by more than 1 level at every zoom above and in exports, for a turn, a skew, a distort and a 3D tip; a coloured layer's edge stays smooth (antialiased) and does not grow a lighter or darker rim either, measured.
No change to how an UNturned layer draws (a render test holds it byte for byte), and the 12 MP / 10 layer re-render stays inside its 16 ms budget (perf note in the commit).
A render test in PhotonzRenderTests with the white-on-white turned and reshaped layer, so this cannot come back.
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Cause: a bitmap with straight alpha (alphaInfo 3, every PNG decode) or no alpha, resampled past its own edge, comes out darker than either side; a premultiplied bitmap of the same colour never does. Evidence: same layer premultiplied reads 0, through a PNG reads 30, and a crop inset from the edge reads 0 because the sampler reads real pixels. Not transparent black from the 2D turn alone, and not the canvas downscale. Core Image's exact internal order was not established; the half-covered arithmetic I first guessed did not hold (peak 30, not 35).

Chose clamping the edge once in wrapped() over an intermediate before each turn because it costs no extra pass or memory and also covers groups, half-pixel layers and shrunk layers, which a turn-only fix would miss. It is in the shared renderer, so Current changes too: the task says next, but the user's own report looks like Current and the renderer cannot differ by release.

Open: reproduced 79 percent only with next-crisp-zoom off (63 levels vs the user's 53), line 3 to 5 device pixels wide vs their 1 to 2. That flag exists only in Next and their title bar read Photonz (Dev), so Current is inferred, not observed. Audit asks them to check their own picture.

left rough: render(scale:) at a scale that misses whole pixels leaves the canvas's last row and column part covered, on an unturned layer too (probe: 0.79 read 202 off over 1466 px, 0.25 read 255 over 464). Not this seam. The Export sheet offers only 1x and 2x so a person cannot reach it; AgentWork passes a scale, not checked whether fractional. Did not earn a task.

Thin line gone: DocumentRenderer.wrapped holds each bitmap's edge. Real app at Next defaults, levels off white along the outline: 25% 31 to 0, 50% 64 to 0, export 1x 64 to 0, the rest 0; with next-crisp-zoom off 79% 63 to 0, 100% 46 to 0. TurnedEdgeSeamTests plus a-turned-layer-has-no-seam-walk; Scripts/test.sh exit 0; 12MP/10-layer edit 7.8ms.
